Subject: A product matching an existing material
Value: Grade under that material
Reason: A new material only where the polymer x filler x variant-class combination does not exist. Bambu's product-level rows stay their own materials. Owner ruling, 2026-09-18.

Subject: Documents in scope
Value: Manufacturer PDFs, web and viewer TDS captured as PDF, scanned sheets via OCR, retailer copies and retailer-only brands
Reason: Everything the corpus publishes is imported; H2C compatibility and price are filters applied later, not an import criterion. Owner ruling, 2026-09-18.

Subject: How much of a sheet is transcribed
Value: Everything it publishes
Reason: Property tables, print settings, qualitative notes, chemical, flammability, certification and composition statements. Owner ruling, 2026-09-18.

Subject: How the estimate stage is handled
Value: Import against the core; scale the model in parallel
Reason: Every batch validates with --no-estimates and with the full build while it runs. Publishing v2 waits for the model work; the import does not. Owner ruling, 2026-09-18.

Subject: ABS-AF
Value: ABS with an aramid fibre load
Reason: Spectrum ABS Kevlar states "based on ABS with the addition of aramid fibers". No material holds ABS x aramid, and aramid is not carbon or glass: it is tough and light and does not raise stiffness the way they do, so filing it under either would move both families. schema/vocab/modifiers.csv gains "Aramid fibre" with this batch.

Subject: ASA-AF
Value: ASA with an aramid fibre load
Reason: Spectrum ASA Kevlar states "a combination of ASA copolymer and aramid fibres". Same reasoning as R005.

Subject: PLA-EC
Value: PLA with an electrically conductive load
Reason: Spectrum PLA Conductive states it is electrically conductive, which is not the same claim as an ESD formulation: a conductive load carries current, an antistatic one only dissipates it, and the database already separates them by what the sheet claims. schema/vocab/modifiers.csv gains "Electrically conductive" with this batch.

Subject: ASA-EC
Value: ASA with an electrically conductive load
Reason: Spectrum ASA Conductive, the sheet states "Electrically Conductive". Same reasoning as R007.

Subject: PETG-PTFE
Value: PETG with a PTFE load
Reason: Spectrum PETG/PTFE names the filler in the product name. PTFE is a tribological additive: it lowers friction and wear and does not reinforce, so it is neither a fibre nor a decorative particle. schema/vocab/modifiers.csv gains "PTFE" with this batch.

Subject: PC-PTFE
Value: PC with a PTFE load
Reason: Spectrum PC/PTFE states "polycarbonate-based (PC) composite filament with the addition of PTFE". Same reasoning as R009.

Subject: PA6-CE
Value: PA6 with a ceramic load
Reason: Spectrum PA6 CS20 FR V0 states a ceramic load in its own description. A ceramic particle load raises density and stiffness and is not a fibre. schema/vocab/modifiers.csv gains "Ceramic" with this batch.

Subject: PLA-ESD
Value: PLA with an ESD formulation
Reason: Spectrum PLA ESD states it is antistatic. ESD formulation is already a modifier value; no material held PLA x ESD.

Subject: PCTG-GF
Value: PCTG with a glass fibre load
Reason: Spectrum PCTG GF10 states "a glass fibres reinforced material based on high-impact PCTG" and publishes 10% glass. PCTG is already a material of its own; no material held PCTG x glass fibre.

Subject: Spectrum S-Flex
Value: TPU
Reason: S-Flex 85A and S-Flex 98A both state "a filament based on a thermoplastic polyether polyurethane", which is TPU. S-Flex 90A and S-Flex Carbon carry the same product name and the same Shore-A hardness scale but name no polymer; they are read as the same line. Recorded by the agent rather than the owner, and open to be overturned.

Subject: PA6-GS
Value: PA6 with a hollow glass sphere load
Reason: Spectrum PA6 GK10 states "Filled with hollow glass spheres, it is stiffer". A hollow sphere stiffens a little and lowers density; it does not carry load along a fibre, so filing it under PA6-GF would pull the glass-fibre family towards a material that is not reinforced. schema/vocab/modifiers.csv gains "Glass spheres" with this batch.

Subject: TPU-CF
Value: TPU with a carbon fibre load
Reason: Spectrum S-Flex Carbon states "the flexibility of traditional flex filament with the added strength and durability provided by a 20% carbon fiber reinforcement". Its polymer is TPU by ruling R014; no material held TPU x carbon fibre.

Subject: PC-ASA
Value: A material with no estimate identity
Reason: 3DXMAX PC/ASA is a polycarbonate and ASA blend, which the product name states. The estimate model identifies a blend by its own name and polymers.csv has no row for this one, so the material stands for what its sheet publishes and is not estimated. A row written from a resin producer reference would let it be, and that is the better fix.

Subject: Another maker's finish variant of PLA
Value: File under the finish material that exists
Reason: The database holds PLA Silk, PLA Metal, PLA Marble, PLA Sparkle, PLA Wood, PLA Galaxy and PLA Glow. They are named after Bambu products and two of them already carry other makers' grades (PLA Silk holds Polymaker and eSUN; PETG-CF holds Polymaker and Spectrum). A second material for one identity is the failure D44 was written about, so another maker's metal-filled PLA joins PLA Metal and its wood joins PLA Wood. Owner ruling, 2026-09-19, replacing the 2026-09-18 answer that asked for generic class materials beside them.

Subject: A sheet that names no polymer
Value: Read the maker's other documents for it, and leave it unregistered where none names it
Reason: A product whose data sheet names no polymer is researched: the maker's safety data sheet or product page usually names it, and that document is fetched, hashed and cited like any other. Where nothing names it, the product stays out of the database rather than entering on an inference. Owner ruling, 2026-09-19.

Subject: A polymer with no row in polymers.csv
Value: Write the row from a fetched reference
Reason: PBT, PCL, PHA, TPS, COC, SEBS, SAN, PA11, LCP, PVC, PBAT and the PPE/PS blend appear in the corpus and the estimate model cannot identify a material without a row for them. Each row is written from a resin producer's or handbook reference that was fetched, hashed and recorded in sources.csv, which is what D35 asks of every other value. Owner ruling, 2026-09-19.

Subject: Spectrum S-Flex Carbon
Value: TPU with a carbon fibre load (TPU-CF)
Reason: Its product line states a thermoplastic polyether polyurethane on the 85A and 98A sheets, and this sheet states "the flexibility of traditional flex filament with a 20% carbon fiber reinforcement". Its published modulus, strength, elongation and heat deflection are a hard composite's, and each is accepted as the sheet's own with the physics finding recorded. Owner ruling, 2026-09-19.

Subject: A publisher name that carries how the document was reached
Value: Move it to Source note
Reason: D71: how a source was reached is a state and a note, not part of the publisher's name. Six sources carry it inside the name and are corrected by migration. Owner ruling, 2026-09-19.

Subject: PLA Metal: a metallic look and a metal-powder load
Value: Split the powder-filled products into their own material
Reason: R039 filed Spectrum PLA Metal Copper, Brass and Bronze under M011 PLA Metal, which holds Bambu PLA Metal. Bambu publishes 1.25 g/cm3, a metallic colour effect; Spectrum publishes 2.28 to 2.36, which is a 60 to 70 per cent metal powder load. One material spanning both taught the density estimate 2.17, a figure neither kind of product measures. R039 is superseded for those three grades. Owner ruling, 2026-09-19.

Subject: Extrudr PLA Basic CF, whose sheet reprints the unfilled table
Value: Register the source and the grade, record no measurements, write a coverage row
Reason: The PLA Basic CF sheet of 04.05.2026 prints the PLA Basic table value for value: modulus, strength, stress at break, elongation, impact, HDT, melting, shrinkage and density are identical and only Hardened Nozzle yes differs, while the prose claims significantly higher rigidity. The product is real and the sheet is the maker own, so both are recorded; its numbers are the unfilled material measurements and are not repeated on a carbon fibre one. A coverage row says so. Owner ruling, 2026-09-19.

Subject: 3DXTECH WearX PA6 Copolymer
Value: Estimate identity PA6
Reason: Its safety data sheet declares CoPolyamide Resin, CAS 25038-54-4, over 95 per cent, the entry 3DXTECH also prints for AmideX PA6 Nylon Copolymer and not the one it prints for PA12. The base is PA6; no document names the comonomer. Its own published values lead, and PA6 fills what it does not publish. Owner ruling, 2026-09-19.

Subject: Spectrum ThermaTech PA and PET-G FX120
Value: ThermaTech PA enters with no Estimate identity; PET-G FX120 stays out
Reason: Neither sheet, nor Spectrum safety data sheets, nor its product pages name a polymer. ThermaTech PA is a polyamide by the maker own filing, so it enters under the Nylon family and nothing is estimated from or for it. PET-G FX120 says only product based on a modified polyester, and its 14 MPa yield with 400 per cent elongation reads as an elastomer, so its name contradicts its numbers and it stays in the ledger until a Spectrum document names the polymer. Owner ruling, 2026-09-19.

Subject: 3DXTECH Obsidian, CarbonX Nylon Gen3 and SimuBone
Value: Obsidian PA6-CF; CarbonX Gen3 PA6 copolymer with carbon fibre; SimuBone PLA with an undisclosed filler
Reason: Read from documents fetched and hashed for the purpose: the Obsidian safety data sheet is titled Obsidian PA6+CF 3D Printing Filament and its product identifier is Obsidian PA6+Carbon Fiber; the CarbonX product page states CarbonX PA6+CF filament is formulated using a PA6 copolymer reinforced with high-modulus carbon fiber, and its safety data sheet gives CAS 25038-54-4; the SimuBone safety data sheet gives Chemical Name Polylactic Acid (PLA) and PLA Resin greater than 85 per cent. SimuBone carries an undisclosed filler that lifts its modulus to 3.41 GPa, so its grade is a Variant and does not pull the PLA family. Owner ruling, 2026-09-19.

Subject: The Obsidian data sheet second column
Value: It is Markforged Onyx, a competitor, and none of its numbers are this product
Reason: The table header reads Obsidian, Onyx. A reader that took the second column for a Z direction would record 37 MPa, 2.4 GPa, 25 per cent, 71 MPa and 3.0 GPa as this product values. Only the first column is the product; the sheet also states Density ASTM D792 1.2 g/cc. Owner ruling, 2026-09-19.
